setup: Marginal cost is the derivative of the cost function \(C(x) = [[a]]x^{2} + [[b]]x + [[c]]\), evaluated at \(x = [[x0]]\).

steps.say: Differentiate term by term: the derivative of \([[a]]x^{2}\) is \(2 \cdot [[a]] x = [[two_a]]x\), of \([[b]]x\) is \([[b]]\), and the constant [[c]] drops out, so \(C'(x) = [[two_a]]x + [[b]]\).

answer: So the marginal cost at \(x = [[x0]]\) is [[marginal]]: the cost of one more unit there.
